s: Curiosity-driven inquiry is a characteristic of which of the following?
x: Basic research is curiosity-driven; applied research addresses a set problem and technology produces products and processes.

s: What is turning an invention into value in the market or society called?
x: Innovation turns an invention (the first creation of a product or process) into market or social value.

s: Science is described as 'know-why'. How is technology described?
x: Science is know-why and gives laws and theories; technology is know-how and gives products and processes.

s: What is the first creation of a new product or process called?
x: Invention is the first creation of a product or process; innovation makes it useful in the market or society.

s: What is research that solves a set problem called?
x: Applied research solves a set problem; basic research is curiosity-driven and translational research takes lab results to use.

s:
Consider the following statements about science and technology:
1. The output of science is laws and theories.
2. The output of technology is products and processes.
3. Translational research is curiosity-driven.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Science yields laws and theories and technology yields products and processes; curiosity-driven research is basic research, while translational research takes lab results to use.

s:
With reference to Digital Embossing Technology, consider the following statements:
I. It is a printing technology that does not use chemicals, solvents and also emits no pollutants.
II. II. It can be used to produce braille maps for the visually challenged.
III. It was introduced in India recently by the National Atlas & Thematic Mapping Organisation (NATMO) functioning as the Attached Office of the Department of Science & Technology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Digital embossing is raised touch printing with no chemicals or solvents and is used for braille maps, so statements I and II are correct. The notes do not cover statement III (NATMO introduction), but the answer given is I, II and III.

s: Which of these is the science of analyzing physical or behavioral characteristics specific to each individual to authenticate their identity?
x: Biometrics identifies a person by unique physical or behavioural traits such as fingerprint, iris, voice or gait. The other options are not identification sciences.

s: Digital embossing is particularly useful for producing which of the following for persons with visual impairment?
x: Digital embossing produces raised tactile printing and is used for braille maps for visually impaired persons.

s: What is the process of building an object layer by layer from a digital model known as?
x: Three-dimensional printing is an additive manufacturing process in which an object is constructed layer by layer from a digital model.

s: FASTag is an example of which technology?

s: Identifying a person by gait or signature is an example of which of the following?
x: Biometrics uses physical traits (fingerprint, iris, face) or behavioural traits (voice, gait, signature).

s: On which technology does a metro smart card work?
x: A metro smart card is a passive NFC card; FASTag is passive RFID.

s: Near Field Communication (NFC) works at 13.56 MHz over what range?
x: NFC works at 13.56 MHz over about 4 cm.

s:
Consider the following statements about RFID:
1. It uses radio waves.
2. It needs a line of sight to the reader.
3. FASTag is a passive RFID tag powered by the toll reader.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: RFID uses radio waves and needs no line of sight; FASTag is a passive RFID tag powered by the toll reader.

s:
Consider the following statements about nanotechnology in India:
1. DST's Nano Science and Technology Initiative (2001) was followed by the Nano Mission in 2007.
2. India has risen from 5th to 3rd in the world in nanoscience publications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2001 Nano Science and Technology Initiative evolved into the Nano Mission (2007). Statement 2 is correct: India rose from 5th to 3rd in nanoscience publications. So 'Both' is right; '1 only' and '2 only' each miss a correct statement, and 'Neither' is wrong.

s: In which year was the Statement on Scientific Temper issued?
x: The Statement on Scientific Temper dates to 1981; 1962 is the Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad and 2013 the Maharashtra Anti-Superstition Act.

s: Which Article asks citizens to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform?
x: Article 51A(h), added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), carries this duty; Nehru popularised the phrase 'scientific temper'.

s: Article 51A(h) on scientific temper was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 51A(h) came with the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the 86th.

s: In which year was the Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad, a scientific temper movement, founded?
x: The Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad was founded in 1962; 1981 is the Statement on Scientific Temper.

s: Which State passed an Anti-Superstition Act in 2013?
x: Maharashtra passed its Anti-Superstition Act in 2013.

s: Who popularised the term 'scientific temper' in The Discovery of India?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru popularised 'scientific temper' in The Discovery of India.

s: What was India's rank in the Network Readiness Index 2024?
x: India ranked 49th in the NRI 2024, up from 79th in 2019; 38th is its GII 2025 rank.

s: When is National Science Day observed in India?
x: National Science Day is observed on 28 February.

s: Which DST scheme is meant only for girl students of Classes 9-12 in STEM?
x: Vigyan Jyoti is for girls only; INSPIRE is open to all young students.

s: What was the first objective of the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2013?
x: The first objective of the STI Policy 2013 was to spread scientific temper in society.

s: Which DST scheme is open to all young students without a competitive exam?
x: INSPIRE of DST covers all young students with no competitive exam; Vigyan Jyoti is only for girls.

s: What is the name of third scientific base in Antarctica?
x: Bharati is India's third Antarctic research station, after Dakshin Gangotri and Maitri, so (2) is correct. The other names are not Indian Antarctic bases.

s: Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh of Jaipur had not built the observatory at
x: Jai Singh II built observatories (Jantar Mantar) at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura. He did not build one at Allahabad, so (4) is correct.

s: The world's highest ground-based telescopic observatory is located at :
x: The Indian Astronomical Observatory at Hanle, India, was billed as the world's highest ground-based telescope site in 2002, and Nepal has no such observatory.

s: Radio Astronomy center is located in |
x: The Radio Astronomy Centre, a facility of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) known for the Ooty Radio Telescope, is located in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, and has been a key facility for radio astronomy research in India since the 1970s.

s: Where is the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) located?
x: GMRT, the world's largest metre-wave telescope with 30 dishes, is at Khodad, about 80 km from Pune, not Ooty.

s: Which institution runs the Udaipur Solar Observatory?
x: PRL, Ahmedabad runs the Udaipur Solar Observatory.

s: Which of the following institution–location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: GMRT is at Khodad near Pune; the Ooty Radio Telescope is at Muthorai.

s: Which institution runs the Ooty Radio Telescope at Muthorai?
x: The Radio Astronomy Centre (Ooty Radio Telescope) at Muthorai belongs to NCRA-TIFR (1969).

s: Which institution runs the Kodaikanal and Kavalur observatories?
x: The Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru, runs the Kodaikanal, Kavalur and Gauribidanur facilities.

s: The Indian School of Mines at Dhanbad was set up mainly for education in which field?
x: The Indian School of Mines (1926), modelled on London's Royal School of Mines, taught mining and applied geology; it became IIT (ISM) in 2016.

s: In which year was the Indian School of Mines, Dhanbad opened?
x: It opened on 9 December 1926 and was made an IIT in 2016.
